clue.text: Alarming surprise set up in a field

definitions.meaning: a sudden upsetting jolt to the feelings
a stook of corn sheaves stood upright together in a harvest field to dry

explanation.surface: Something startling has been staged out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up in a field' reads like a trap or an ambush; it is the farming sense, a bundle of sheaves propped together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a jolt of alarm, and a stook of sheaves stood upright at harvest.

clue.text: Bright mover trained to follow the stars

definitions.text: Bright mover trained to follow the stars

parts.words: Bright mover trained to follow the stars
parts.note: a theatre lamp aimed at, or trained on, the leading performers as they move across the stage

explanation.surface: A clever creature taught to steer by celestial bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests astronomy and navigation; they are the lead actors, and 'trained' means aimed, not taught.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre lamp throws a beam that tracks the leading performers on stage.

clue.text: Here singers work overtime

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed above the other

parts.note: op is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Singers on stage put in extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overtime' splits into 'over' and 'time': OP sits over ERA in the down entry. The definition is 'Here singers', the place where singers perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Singers perform in sung drama, the art form staged in theatres for vocalists.

clue.text: Hangman out of bed dressing for dinner

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner whose name became a byword for hangman
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: The executioner rises and gets dressed for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing for dinner' looks like putting on smart clothes; it is a sauce. Ketch was the hangman's nickname in England after Jack Ketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato sauce is a condiment, a dressing poured over food.

clue.text: Status achieved by nodding a lot

definitions.text: Status achieved by nodding a lot

parts.words: Status achieved by nodding a lot
parts.note: at an auction a bidder nods to the auctioneer, and the winning nod brings possession of the item for sale, called a lot

explanation.surface: Someone who agrees with everyone climbs the social ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like 'very often', but it is an auction lot; 'nodding' is how a bidder signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning the bid on a lot gives the bidder the legal standing of possessing it.

clue.text: World in Action demonstrator?

parts.note: a clockwork model that shows the planets, worlds, moving round the sun

explanation.surface: Someone presenting a current affairs television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: World in Action was a British television documentary series; here the worlds are planets set in motion by a mechanical model.
explanation.definitionFit: A geared model of the solar system demonstrates the planets in their orbits.

clue.text: Novel way of losing eleven days

definitions.meaning: a fresh manner of doing something
Britain's move to the Gregorian calendar in 1752 skipped eleven days, from 2 to 14 September

explanation.surface: A new approach that somehow cost someone nearly two weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1752 Britain switched calendars and dropped eleven days; dates by the new calendar are called this, as against Old Style.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh manner, literally; and the name for dates reckoned by the Gregorian calendar adopted in 1752.

clue.text: Polish picture of a fateful stream

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it
an icon is a sacred picture

explanation.surface: Someone shines up a painting of a doom-laden river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb. Caesar crossed this stream in 49 BC, committing himself to civil war.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossed this Italian stream in 49 BC, a point of no return, hence fateful.

clue.text: Tough quality impairs S.M.'s power on parade?

definitions.meaning: being burly and strong, like a big hardy dog or man
hoarseness weakens a sergeant major's shouted commands on the parade ground

explanation.surface: Something hard spoils a sergeant major's authority at drill.
explanation.walkthrough: S.M. is sergeant major; a croaky voice would sap his bellowed orders. Husky means both burly and hoarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Husky means both brawny and hoarse-voiced, so the quality covers sturdiness and a croaky throat.

clue.text: Paper sticker for 'Keep Britain Tidy " campaign

definitions.text: Paper sticker for 'Keep Britain Tidy " campaign

parts.words: Paper sticker for 'Keep Britain Tidy " campaign
parts.note: a pointed spike that stabs waste paper, as used by litter collectors in an anti-litter drive

explanation.surface: An adhesive label printed for the national anti-litter campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticker' looks like a label; it is a thing that sticks, pierces, paper. Keep Britain Tidy is a British anti-litter campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike or tine on a litter-picker's stick pierces stray paper.

clue.text: Outcome of armed force-run for it

definitions.meaning: the toppling of a government, a coup, as the result of military action
in cricket, an extra run scored when a fielder's throw at the stumps goes past and is not stopped

explanation.surface: A military coup ends with everyone being told to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run for it' reads as a call to escape; it is cricket, where a wild throw from the field lets batsmen take a further run.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime's downfall by force is its toppling; in cricket the word names a stray throw and the run it gives.

clue.text: Fish, love, in the deepest part

parts.note: the bass is a fish
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone fondly addresses a fish that lives at the very bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The deepest part' suggests the bottom of the sea, where fish live; it is the lowest voice part in music.
explanation.definitionFit: In singing, the lowest male voice or line is the bass, Italian basso.

clue.text: Cooper's novel type of calf hide?

definitions.meaning: James Fenimore Cooper wrote a series of frontier tales named after his hero Natty Bumppo's nickname
a stocking made of leather covers, or hides, the calf of the leg

explanation.surface: A novelist's book describes a particular kind of calfskin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calf hide' looks like calfskin leather; read 'hide' as a verb, something that conceals the calf of the leg. Cooper is the American novelist James Fenimore Cooper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooper's frontier novels are the tales named for his buckskin hero; and leggings of leather cover the lower leg.

clue.text: Surly parliament purged in gay, if heartless, circumstances

indicators.note: circumstances literally means things standing around, so the outer letters surround the parliament
the word gay loses its middle letter, its heart, keeping only the outside pair

parts.note: the Rump Parliament was what remained of the Long Parliament after Pride's Purge of 1648

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered assembly is cleansed in cheerful though cold-hearted conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle of GAY to leave GY; 'circumstances', in its literal sense of standing around, puts that pair round RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Surly and grumpy are synonyms, both meaning sullen and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Life-line not on hand-mark where it was

definitions.text: Life-line not on hand-mark where it was

parts.words: Life-line not on hand-mark where it was
parts.note: the cord that fed the baby before birth, not the life line of palmistry; the scar left where it was attached

explanation.surface: A palm reader notes a life line missing from the hand, with a mark showing where it once ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life-line' suggests palm reading, but the hand is ruled out: it is the cord joining an unborn baby to its mother, and the mark is the navel.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel is the scar left where the cord once joined the foetus to the placenta.

clue.text: He swore they had brought him a mare (Smollett)

definitions.text: He swore they had brought him a mare (Smollett)

parts.words: He swore they had brought him a mare (Smollett)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Smollett's History of England reports Henry VIII complaining about his bride Anne of Cleves, naming her homeland

explanation.surface: A line from Smollett: a man furiously claims he was given a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash before 'mare'; fill it. Henry VIII, disappointed by Anne of Cleves, was said to call her a mare from her home region in the Low Countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne of Cleves came from the Low Countries, the region that gave Henry VIII's insult its place name.

clue.text: Is nimbly evasive at the tradesmen's entrance

definitions.meaning: dodges deftly out of the way
the stairs at the side door of a grand house, used by delivery men

explanation.surface: A delivery man dodges about at the back door of a big house.
explanation.walkthrough: The tradesmen's entrance was the side door of a large house kept for deliveries and servants; its stairs give the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging nimbly is the verb; the steps by a house's side door are the noun phrase.

clue.text: Extol the dance that is seen in the meadow

definitions.text: that is seen in the meadow

parts.note: to puff something is to praise it extravagantly
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Praise the folk dance being performed out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a round white fungus found in grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A round fungus common in grassland that bursts to release spores.

clue.text: They are still presented with vivid effect

definitions.text: They are still presented with vivid effect

parts.words: They are still presented with vivid effect
parts.note: motionless scenes posed by living people, the French ... vivants, living pictures

explanation.surface: Things are nevertheless shown off with striking impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'nevertheless'; it means motionless. 'Vivid' nods to vivants in the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux vivants are silent motionless scenes staged by costumed performers.

clue.text: Charm of our appearance with mane unruly

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the two parts are joined
an unruly mane is tangled, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Our good looks, and an untamed head of hair, are attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges MANE to give ENAM; 'our' is taken as it is, 'appearance' meaning it shows up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to captivate or bewitch, as charm does.

clue.text: Ran after two little boys

parts.note: Chas is a short form of the boy's name Charles
Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted behind a pair of small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two little boys' gives two shortened names, CHAS and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue someone is to run after them.

clue.text: Impetuous recipient of coals of fire ?

definitions.text: Impetuous recipient of coals of fire ?

parts.words: Impetuous recipient of coals of fire ?
parts.note: a rash person; the Bible speaks of heaping coals of fire on someone's head, which would make that head hot

explanation.surface: A rash person is repaid with kindness for wrongs done.
explanation.walkthrough: Heaping coals of fire on someone's head (Proverbs, Romans) means shaming them with kindness; taken literally it heats the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered person acts without thinking, like one whose temper is easily fired.

clue.text: Poor Hilda, a Mexican beauty

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Hilda, a lovely woman from Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges HILDA and A. The beauty is a flower native to Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy garden flower native to Mexico, a beauty of the border.

clue.text: Their denominators may be common, too

definitions.text: Their denominators may be common, too

parts.words: Their denominators may be common, too
parts.note: ordinary fractions written with a number below the line, which can share a lowest common denominator, and whose name also means common

explanation.surface: A remark about the shared bottom numbers of some sums.
explanation.walkthrough: The fractions are called common as well as their other name, and that name also means coarse or common, hence 'too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and improper fractions written as a numerator over a denominator are the common, unrefined kind.

clue.text: Goddess, a potential 20

definitions.meaning: the Roman goddess of the hearth
a wax match, which has a head that will become hot when struck

explanation.surface: A deity who could turn into a hothead.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the answer to 20-down; a match is a potential one because its head becomes hot when struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman hearth goddess, and also an old name for a short wax match, which has a head that gets hot.

clue.text: Overhead, a swarm of bees — too fat to run?

parts.note: O stands for over in cricket bowling figures, and here it goes at the head of the down entry

indicators.note: a swarm is a disordered mass, so the letters of bees are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cloud of bees flies above, but someone is too heavy to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' splits as over plus head: O, the cricket abbreviation for over, goes at the top. 'A swarm of' rearranges BEES to BESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being grossly overweight would leave someone too heavy to run.

clue.text: A prong needed to make this mural decoration stick

definitions.text: A prong needed to make this mural decoration stick

parts.words: A prong needed to make this mural decoration stick
parts.note: wall painting done on dry plaster, which gives paint no grip unless the surface is keyed, roughened with a pointed tool

explanation.surface: A craftsman explains that a spike is needed to fix a wall painting in place.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlike true fresco on wet plaster, this kind of mural is painted on dry plaster, so the wall has to be roughened to give the paint a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for dry, secco is wall painting applied to plaster that has already set.

clue.text: Eels learn to wriggle-excellent !

indicators.note: eels wriggle, so the letters of the two words writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: Eels are taught to squirm, and the result is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To wriggle' rearranges EELS LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of approval meaning everything is fine, from the old watchman's call.

clue.text: Move as a ritual into the country

indicators.note: move here means shift around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shifts ceremonially into the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges AS A RITUAL; 'into' just joins it to 'the country'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation and continent in the southern hemisphere, a country by any measure.

clue.text: Don clothes and get in line

definitions.meaning: the military order for soldiers to align themselves in their ranks

explanation.surface: Get changed and then join the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get in line' sounds like queueing; it is the parade-ground command for soldiers to line up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on garments is one sense; soldiers aligning in ranks on command is the other.
